Therefore, Tambor must have been born by approximately 97 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. |death=[[19 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' [[Mustafar]]{{Film|III}} |species=[[Skakoan]]{{Databank|wat-tambor|Wat Tambor}} |gender=[[Gender|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.98 [[meter]]s {{C|6 [[Foot|ft]], 6 in}}''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]'' |mass= |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color|Black]]{{Film|II}} |skin=Green |cyber= |families=[[Tambors]][[Darth Vader (2020) 29|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 29]] |parents= |partners= |siblings= |children=[[Wat Tambor II]] |affiliation=*[[Techno Union]] **[[Baktoid Armor Workshop]]''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' *[[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] **[[Executive Separatist Council]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Wat Tambor spoils for others what he cannot possess.|Cham Syndulla|{{TCW|Liberty on Ryloth}}}} '''Wat Tambor''' was a [[Gender|male]] [[Skakoan]] who was the [[foreman]] of the [[Techno Union]] and an executive of [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]]. During the [[Separatist Crisis]], he pledged the Techno Union's resources to the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]], earning himself a seat on the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] during the [[Clone Wars]]. In the conflict's early stages, Tambor was appointed [[Emir of Ryloth]] and supervised its [[Battle of Ryloth|occupation]] by the Separatists, which was fiercely resisted by local [[Twi'lek]] [[Twi'lek Resistance|freedom fighters]] led by [[Cham Syndulla]]. After defying orders to abandon [[Ryloth]] when the tide of battle turned against the Separatists, Tambor was left behind and captured by the [[Galactic Republic]]. He was briefly [[Prison|imprisoned]] on [[Coruscant]] before being liberated later in the conflict. As the Clone Wars escalated, Wat Tambor took an interest in the captive [[Advanced Recon Commando|ARC trooper]] [[Echo]], who had been captured during a [[Battle of Lola Sayu|battle]] in the [[Citadel]] but was presumed [[Death|dead]] by the Republic. Tambor kept an unconscious Echo in a [[stasis chamber]] and managed to extract information from Echo's mind to use as an [[Rex's battle strategy algorithm|algorithm]] consisting of strategies devised by Echo and the [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]]. While officially professing the Techno Union's neutrality, Tambor had sold the algorithm to the Separatist [[Admiral]] [[Trench]], who used it to great effect during the [[Battle of Anaxes]] to invade the Republic world of [[Anaxes]]. Tambor's dealings with the Separatists were exposed by a Republic infiltration team consisting of Rex, [[Clone Force 99]], and the [[Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]]. During the final [[Standard day|days]] of the Clone Wars, Wat Tambor and the rest of the Separatist Council relocated from the planet [[Utapau]] to [[Mustafar]], where they were [[Mission to Mustafar|slaughtered]] by [[Darth]] Vader in the conflict immediate aftermath. Following his demise, the newly-formed [[Galactic Empire]] assumed control of the Techno Union's assets. ==Biography== ===Foreman of the Union=== {{Quote|I-its all here. Wat Tambor acquired your personality matrix nearly a century ago. Wanted to study it. I think he was obsessed with you.|Doctor Aphra, to 0-0-0|[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 16|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 16]]}} A [[Gender|male]] [[Skakoan]] from the [[planet]] [[Skako]], Wat Tambor was [[Reproduction|born]] by circa 97 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]]. He left his [[homeworld]] at an early age and began a career in technology on the harsh industrial planet of [[Metalorn]]. He eventually became [[foreman]] of the [[Techno Union]], a powerful commercial body that made massive profits from developing new technologies, and an executive of [[Baktoid Armor Workshop]], an arms manufacturer. As a result, Tambor became very wealthy. Tambor also had a son, [[Wat Tambor II]], who went into [[politics]] and became a member of the [[Ruling Council (Skako Minor)|Skakoan Ruling Council]]. Nearly a century before the [[Galactic Civil War]], Tambor acquired the [[Triple-Zero protocol personality matrix]] with the intent of studying it. ===The Separatist Crisis=== {{Quote|The Techno Union army…is at your disposal, Count.|Wat Tambor, during the secret Separatist meeting on Geonosis|}} [[File:WatTambor-AOTC.png|thumb|left|250px|Wat Tambor convened with the rest of the Separatist Council on Geonosis to pledge his battle droids to Count Dooku.]] During the last [[Standard year|years]] of the [[Galactic Republic]], Tambor supported the [[Separatist Crisis|Secessionist Movement]], which eventually developed into the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]. During the Separatist Crisis, Wat Tambor and several other pro-Separatist corporate leaders, including the [[Trade Federation]] [[Viceroy]] [[Nute Gunray]], the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]] [[Chairman]] [[San Hill]], and the [[Commerce Guild]] president [[Shu Mai]] attended a secret conference on the planet [[Geonosis]] that was hosted by the Separatist leader [[Count]] [[Dooku]] and the [[Geonosian]] [[Archduke]] [[Poggle the Lesser]], who oversaw the production of [[battle droid]]s for the Techno Union.{{SWE|characters|pogglethelesser|Poggle the Lesser}} At the meeting, Tambor [[Geonosian accord|pledged]] the Techno Union's resources to the Separatist cause. During the ensuing [[First Battle of Geonosis]], the first battle of the [[Clone Wars]], Wat Tambor and other Separatist delegates watched the fighting unfold through a [[holotable]] in the [[Geonosian War Room]] before fleeing Geonosis to escape the advancing [[Grand Army of the Republic]]. Despite the Techno Union's support for the Separatist cause, the company still declared neutrality{{TCW|On the Wings of Keeradaks}} and was even represented in the [[Galactic Senate]] by [[Senator]] [[Gume Saam]].{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}} At some point after he joined the CIS, Tambor flew [[Wat Tambor's Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter|his]] ''[[Belbullab-22 heavy starfighter]] near an orange astronomical object.{{FFGXW2|set=Servants of Strife Squadron Pack|cardname=Wat Tambor}} ===The Clone Wars=== ====Battle on Quarmendy==== {{Quote|Sir, we have incoming. One of our own--though it's incoming very fast."''
''"What do you mean one of our…oh no.|A battle droid and Wat Tambor, as another battle droid crashes into them|[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 2|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 2]]}} Early in the war, Tambor led Separatist forces to capture the planet [[Quarmendy]] and its important trading post the [[Nexus]], coming to rule over it as an [[emir]]. A Republic counterattack to retake the Nexus was led by [[Plo Koon]] and [[Clone Commander]] [[Wolffe]], with the [[Jedi Master]] leading a starfighter assault in order to distract Tambor from a smaller attack mounted by Wolffe, who planned to lead a squad of clones with jet packs onto the station's surface. Due to the impregnable nature of the Nexus, Tambor was surprised that the Republic would dare to launch such an operation but he nonetheless ordered his [[Vulture-class starfighter|vulture droids]] to be scrambled in order to fend off Plo's starfighters. He then confronted the former custodian of the Nexus, [[Orkle]], accusing her of trying to undermine his control of the station. He warned her that her life meant very little to him, but stated that she would make a good hostage to use against the Republic. As the battle for the skies intensified, Wolffe and his clones began their attack on the station's surface but came under heavy fire from gun turrets. Informed of this maneuver, Tambor took the news in his stride and ordered a unit of [[D1-series aerial battle droid]]s out to engage the clones in the air before they could land. Unfortunately for Tambor, however, Wolffe was able to attach a [[thermal detonator]] to one of the droids before sending it spiralling towards the Skakoan's command centre. Tambor was able to escape the resulting explosion, holding onto Orkle as his hostage, but was immediately confronted by Wolffe and the clones who demanded his surrender and her release. Tambor declared that he would rather blow the Nexus apart than surrender it, pressing a detonator he had kept on his person before grabbing onto two D1 battle droids and making his escape. Wolffe was left to rescue Orkle, but neither he nor Plo were able to save the station from Tambor's detonation and it was blown apart. ====Emir of Ryloth==== {{Quote|My ship!|Wat Tambor, as TA-175 takes his ship|}} [[File:Tambor_on_Ryloth.png|250px|thumb|Emir Tambor with Separatist forces on Ryloth]] After his escape from Quarmendy, Tambor spearheaded the Separatist [[Battle of Ryloth|invasion]] of [[Ryloth]], the homeworld of the [[Twi'lek]] [[species]], and supervised its subsequent occupation{{SWE|characters|wattambor|Wat Tambor}} after being installed as the [[Emir of Ryloth]] by Count Dooku. Setting up headquarters in the [[capital]] [[city]] of [[Lessu City|Lessu]], the Skakoan and his [[tactical droid]] [[TA-175]] ruled the planet with an iron fist and many Twi'leks starved as a result of the Separatist occupation. Ryloth was also blockaded by a large Separatist war fleet to deter any Republic attempts to retake Ryloth. When the Senate dispatched reinforcements to retake Ryloth, Tambor ordered the [[Neimoidian]] [[Captain]] [[Mar Tuuk]] to prevent a Republic invasion of the planet.{{TCW|Storm Over Ryloth}} Shortly later, three [[Republic Navy]] [[Venator-class Star Destroyer|''Venator''-class Star Destroyers]] under the command of [[Jedi General]] and [[Jedi Knight|Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen]] emerged from hyperspace. However, Tuuk trapped the Star Destroyers by sending four [[Munificent-class star frigate|''Munificent''-class star frigates]] to interdict them. As a result of this counter-attack, the ''Venator'' Star Destroyer ''[[Redeemer]]'' was crippled while another ship, the ''[[Defender]]'', was badly damaged. Via [[hologram]], Tambor congratulated Tuuk on his success but warned him not to under-estimate General Skywalker since the Techno Union foreman knew how he caused nothing but trouble for Count Dooku and the Separatist Alliance. Despite the initial setback, General Skywalker used the crippled ''Defender'' to ram into Tuuk's flagship, a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|Droid Control Ship]]. Republic reinforcements under [[Jedi Master]]s [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Mace Windu]] then exited hyperspace with three [[Acclamator-class transgalactic military assault ship|''Acclamator''-class transgalactic military assault ships]] carrying substantial ground forces to liberate Ryloth. In response to the planned Republic landings at the Ryloth city of [[Nabat]], Tambor ordered the tactical droid [[TX-20]] to use captive Twi'leks as 'living shields' to deter the Republic's [[clone trooper]]s and their Jedi commanders from launching a heavy attack. As the Republic's [[Ghost Company]] advanced into Nabat, TX-20 unleashed several starved [[gutkurr]]s but the Jedi and clones managed to foil this attack. The capture of Nabat enabled the clone army to march on Lessu.{{TCW|Innocents of Ryloth}} [[File:TA175Tambor-LoR.png|thumb|left|250px|Tambor confers with TA-175]] In response to Master Windu's advance on Lessu, [[Emir]] Tambor conferred with TA-175. Despite the odds stacked against him, he refused to order a retreat and claimed that Windu did not have sufficient troops to retake the city. Tambor also ordered that all droids be brought into Lessu in order to secure his stronghold and the strategically important plasma bridge. By this stage, Republic starfighters under General Skywalker had secured the space around Ryloth and General Kenobi had taken the [[Jixuan desert]], allowing the planet's southern hemisphere to fall under Republic control. In response to Tambor's military presence in Lessu, Mace Windu decided to enlist the help of the [[Twi'lek Resistance]] under [[Cham Syndulla]]. Later, Wat Tambor and TA-175 conferred with Count Dooku, who ordered the Techno Union foreman to retreat with whatever valuables he could and destroy everything else. While Tambor was alarmed by Dooku's order, the Count explained that he wanted to use Ryloth to demonstrate the cost of a "Republic victory" to the galaxy. As Republic forces closed in on Lessu, Tambor ordered TA-175 to prepare his shuttle for departure. Tambor refused to leave until the last of Ryloth's treasures had been loaded onto his shuttle. This infuriated Count Dooku who wanted him out of the city before Republic reinforcements arrived. The Separatist leader intended to use several [[Hyena-class Droid Fighter/Bomber|''Hyena''-class Droid Bombers]] to bomb Lessu as part of a "scorched earth" tactic and did not want the Republic to gain a valuable prisoner. [[File:Windu_corners_Tambor.png|thumb|left|250px|Emir Tambor cornered by Mace Windu]] In a desperate attempt to slow down Windu and Cham's advance, Tambor attempted to use Twi'lek civilians as living shields. Despite his best efforts, the Republic and their Twi'lek allies managed to secure control of the plasma bridge and liberate the city. Before Tambor could reach his shuttle, TA-175 departed on the ship with his looted treasures; leaving Tambor to be captured by Master Windu and Cham's forces. Despite Tambor's capture, Count Dooku gave the order for the Hyena bombers to raze Lessu to the ground. When confronted by Windu, the captive Tambor told him that they would perish for the glory of the Separatist cause. However, Dooku's Hyena bombers were knocked out of the sky by Anakin and his [[Padawan]] [[Ahsoka Tano]]'s [[starfighter]]s. Defeated, Tambor surrendered unconditionally to the clone [[trooper]]s and Cham's Twi'lek Resistance forces. ====Republic incarceration==== Following his capture on Ryloth, Tambor was incarcerated in the [[Imperial Inspectorate HQ|Republic Center for Military Operations]] on [[Coruscant]]. Poggle the Lesser was also imprisoned in the center,{{TCW|The Jedi Who Knew Too Much}} with [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic]] mentioning him to Poggle by asking if the foreman had been the one to create the plans for a [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|mobile battle station]] the Archduke was a part of.''[[Catalyst: A Rogue One Novel]]'' Tambor remained under Republic custody during Ahsoka Tano's [[Escape from the Republic military base|escape]] from the same facility. ====Dealing with the "Bad Batch"==== {{Quote|They've ruined ''years'' of research!|Wat Tambor, as he inspects the remains of his experiment|}} [[File:Rex_algorithm.png|thumb|250px|Skywalker, Captain Rex, and the "Bad Batch" were obstacles to Tambor's plans involving the strategy algorithm.]] Tambor later escaped from the detention center, the details of his escape were redacted by [[Clone Intelligence]].{{GermanFanCite|121|Database}} Free from Republic custody, the foreman rejoined the Separatist war effort, retreating to the Techno Union's headquarters in [[Purkoll]], a city on the planet [[Skako Minor]]. At some point, Tambor obtained captured [[Advanced Recon Commando|ARC trooper]] [[Echo]], designated CT-1409, who had been presumed [[Death|killed]] during a [[Battle of Lola Sayu|mission]] to the [[Citadel]] on [[Lola Sayu]]. Holding Echo within a [[stasis chamber]], Tambor used the unconscious clone trooper to make [[Rex's battle strategy algorithm|strategy algorithm]] which fed the Separatist Admiral [[Trench]] information on the Republic's tactics during the [[Battle of Anaxes]].{{TCW|A Distant Echo}} Using the algorithm, the Separatist tactics matched plans created by [[Clone Captain]] [[Rex]] and Echo.{{TCW|The Bad Batch (episode)}} With their strategy algorithm, Admiral Trench won several victories on Anaxes and seemed poised to conquer the planet. In response, Rex and a group of defective clone troopers known as the [[Clone Force 99|"Bad Batch"]] infiltrated a Separatist [[Cyber Center]]. During the mission, they discovered a signal originating from Skako Minor, which had declared itself neutral during the Clone Wars, recognized Echo's voice, and deduced that the ARC trooper was still alive. [[File:Skakoantechnician.png|thumb|left|250px|Tambor on Skako Minor with other Skakoans]] Following the clone trooper's attack on the Cyber Center, Admiral Trench contacted Skako Minor. A subordinate of his informed Tambor of of the transmission, and the foreman ordered him to send it through. Trench then appeared on a view screen and warned Tambor that the Republic had traced the algorithm's signal to Skako Minor, cautioning the Skaokan that his operation on the planet could be in jeopardy. Tambor reasoned that, because the Techno Union had corporate neutrality, the Republic would not dare attack them, but Trench asserted that their neutrality did not matter to the Republic operatives. The Skakoan then resolved to stop the clone rescuers. As expected, Rex, the Bad Batch, and Master Skywalker infiltrated Skako Minor. After landing on the planet and making contact with the native [[Poletec]], the Republic infiltrators managed to trace Echo's signal to Purkoll. Inside the facility, they fought and overpowered several of Tambor's [[D1-series aerial battle droid]]s and managed to find Echo in the core systems room. Before they could access the chamber, the clones were contacted via hologram by a gloating Wat Tambor, who informed them that they had stumbled into a trap. He told them that he had used Rex's strategy algorithm to predict every move they had made since their arrival on Skako Minor. When Tambor accused the clones of violating Skako Minor's neutrality, Rex responded that the Techno Union had already violated the planet's neutrality by bringing a Republic prisoner to the planet. Before departing, Tambor praised the clones for doing their part and ordered several D-wing droids to execute the intruders. The clones managed to free Echo from the stasis chamber but found themselves trapped in the tower. By that time, Wat Tambor and several aides had arrived on the facility's ground floor. Tambor ordered his Skakoan associates to prepare the [[S/D Decimator droid|Decimator]], a spherical device capable of attacking the Republic forces. However, Skywalker and the clones managed to escape the Core Systems room through an exhaust tunnel before the Decimator could breach the chamber. A confused Tambor demanded to know why the Decimator shut itself off and then looked through the hole it had cut into the door upon being informed that it could detect no organic matter, only to see that the Republic troops had left a "parting gift" in the form of several thermal detonators planted about the room. Tambor had just enough time to utter "Oh, no" before the explosives detonated in his face, wrecking the core systems room and sending Tambor flying backwards several feet. After entering the damaged room, the foreman was incensed to find Echo, whom he regarded as Techno Union property, missing and the stasis chamber destroyed, ruining what he claimed was years of research. He ordered his forces to locate the Republic group. Despite Tambor's best efforts to capture the intruders, Skywalker and the clones managed to tame several winged [[keeradak]] reptiles and escape to a Poletec village. In response, Wat sent a force of D-wing droids and [[Octuptarra tri-droid|octuptarra magna tri-droids]] to destroy them. However, the clones and their Poletec allies managed to trap them in a valley and defeat them. The surviving D-wing droids retreated and informed Wat of the defeat. The foreman regarded the loss of Echo as a devastating blow to the Techno Union's profit margins and wanted to find a way to recoup on his company's losses. Meanwhile, Skywalker and the clones managed to return with Echo to Anaxes where the Republic devised a plan to defeat Admiral Trench's invasion.{{TCW|Unfinished Business (episode)}} Despite the serious breach of security on Skako Minor, Tambor stated he would eventually inform the Separatists of the loss of Echo. However, during the closing acts of the battle for Anaxes, Tambor had yet to do so. With the help of Skywalker, Rex and the "Bad Batch," Echo managed to fake a signal from Skako Minor and feed Trench with false strategies. The Separatist Admiral dispatched most of his forces to secure the main [[Anaxes assembly complex|Republic assembly plant]] on Anaxes. This enabled Echo to deactivate them. The Republic and Jedi then managed to defuse one of Trench's bombs, kill the Admiral, and destroy his fleet. As a result, the Republic scored a victory on Anaxes. ====Last days of the Confederacy==== {{Quote|When my new apprentice Darth Vader arrives, he will…take care of you.|Darth Sidious, to the Separatist Council|}} [[File:Vader_and_Tambor_DB.png|thumb|225px|Tambor, seconds before being slain by Darth Vader]] Following the [[Battle of Coruscant]], which saw the death of Count Dooku at the hands of General Skywalker, Wat Tambor and the [[Executive Separatist Council|Separatist Council]] met with the Separatist military leader [[General]] [[Grievous]] on the sinkhole world of [[Utapau]]. Tambor and the Separatist Council later relocated to a protective stronghold on the [[Volcano|volcanic]] world of [[Mustafar]], whose [[Mustafarian|natives]] had a trade agreement with the Techno Union and mined unique and valuable minerals from the planet's [[Magma|lava]] rivers on its behalf while Grievous was [[Battle of Utapau|killed]].{{Databank|mustafar|Mustafar}} Darth Sidious then informed the Separatist Council that his new apprentice [[Darth]] Vader would come and accept their surrender. However, Vader, formerly Anakin Skywalker, instead [[Mission to Mustafar|executed]] the Separatist Council. As his peers were cut down, Tambor and [[Rune Haako]] fled into a conference room in an attempt to hide from the Sith Lord but the effort proved futile as Vader cut down Haako before impaling Tambor with his lightsaber.{{Databank|url=emir-wat-tambor-biography-gallery|title=Emir Wat Tambor Biography Gallery}} {{C|Image 10 of 10}} Just moments later, Gunray was killed and the Battle Droids were shut down, ending the Clone Wars. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Tambor was Skako's most cherished son. For us, his personal workshop is a holy site.|[[Hallio Bas]]|[[Doctor Aphra (2016) 15|''Doctor Aphra'' (2016) 15]]}} Following Tambor's death, Vader underwent a [[Mission to Skako Minor (Darth Vader)|Mission to Skako Minor]], where he executed all of Tambor's loyalists[[Darth Vader (2020) 28|''Darth Vader'' (2020) 28]] by wiping out the Ruling Council, including Tambor's son. Vader then installed a [[Skakoan Council|new regime]] loyal to the newly-formed [[Galactic Empire]]. The Empire also assumed control of the former Techno Union's assets.{{Databank|confederacy-of-independent-systems|Confederacy of Independent Systems}} At some point following the [[skirmish aboard the Sorca Retreat]] during the Galactic Civil War, Doctor [[Chelli Lona Aphra|Aphra]] and the [[Son-tuul Pride]] [[Mission to Skako Minor (Son-tuul Pride)|raided]] [[Wat Tambor's workshop]] to find out he had acquired the Triple-Zero protocol [[personality matrix]] almost a [[Standard century|century]] prior. He became interested in studying it, discovered it was too dangerous to be activated, and sent it to [[Quarantine World III]] to be quarantined. Tambor kept the memories of [[0-0-0]] and stored them in the Techno Union databanks as part of the Separatists' Research and Development. After the Clone Wars, the databanks were transferred over to the Empire and shifted into [[Hivebase-1]]. Between [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]],The events of [[Star Wars: Darth Vader (2020)|''Star Wars Darth Vader'' (2020)]] take place after the [[Escape from Cloud City]] and before the [[Rescue of Han Solo]], which are dated to [[3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY]], respectively, by ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''. a [[pirate]] named [[Jul Tambor]] emerged. The grandson of Wat, he engineered a [[blockade of Skako Minor]] to free it from [[Occupation of Skako Minor|Imperial control]]. ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|The Nexus is neutral in galactic politics. But that doesn't mean I can't spot a ruthless coward when I see one.|Orkle, to Wat Tambor|[[Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales 2|''Star Wars Adventures: The Clone Wars – Battle Tales'' 2]]}} Wat Tambor was a Skakoan male who stood at 1.98 [[meter]]s (6 [[Foot|feet]], 6 inches) tall, with [[Color|green]] skin and black [[eye]]s. He required a [[Pressure suit|protective suit]] to survive away from Skako's high pressure atmosphere. The suit included a [[vocabulator]] which could process Skakoan speech. [[File:WatTambor-SWZ.png|thumb|left|300px|Tambor's personal Belbullab-22 starfighter]] Strict and inventive, Wat Tambor had a mind for war machines''[[Star Wars: Galactic Defense]]'' and was one of the original and most fervent Separatist leaders, having pledging his loyalty and the Techno Union's battle droid armies to the Confederacy of Independent Systems after being attracted to the movement by Dooku's promises of unlimited pursuit of profits.{{Databank|retail-caucus-droid|Retail Caucus Droid}} Despite declaring the Techno Union neutral during the Clone Wars, Tambor was an active supporter of the Separatist cause who channeled substantial resources and information to their war effort. On one occasion, he used the drugged clone trooper Echo to provide Admiral Trench with Rex's strategy algorithm, which greatly assisted the Separatist campaign to conquer the Republic world of Anaxes. As a businessman, he was concerned with protecting the Techno Union's profit margins and minimizing losses to his company by all means necessary. [[Orkle]] considered Tambor a ruthless coward. As both a businessman and military commander, Tambor was ruthless and had a disregard for the lives of other sentient beings. During the Separatist occupation of Ryloth, many Twi'leks starved under his rule. During a battle in Nabat, he gave orders for Twi'lek civilians to be used as "living shields" to deter the Republic and Jedi forces. Despite his disregard for sentient lives, Tambor was visibly upset when Skywalker and Clone Force 99 destroyed his laboratory along with its machines and years of research. Like all members of the Separatist Council, Wat Tambor was a corporate tycoon and was greedy as well. He profited off of the war effort like the other council members and exploited other star systems to enrich himself and acquire more wealth. He would often sack various worlds and strip them of their money and treasure to have for himself. Tambor was also a master strategist as he led many campaigns against the Republic during the war and broke out of Republic custody numerous times. Tambor was also authoritarian as whenever he'd conquer a system, he'd rule the planet with an iron fist and often enslave its native population, strip away the planet's money and treasure, and devastate the planet to benefit the cause of the Separatists. At the bidding of Count Dooku, Tambor exercised a "scorched earth" policy towards Ryloth by looting the planet's valuables in order to show the galaxy the "cost" of a Republic victory. However, his avarice cost him dearly when he refused to evacuate Ryloth until the last shipment of valuables had arrived; a decision which contributed to his capture by Master Windu. ==Skills and abilities== Tambor was an accomplished engineer and logistical expert, leading the Techno Union until the end of the Clone War as its foreman. In his role, he utilized ARC trooper Echo to his advantage, holding the clone in a stasis chamber on Skako Minor and relied on the unconscious trooper transmitting a strategy algorithm to Admiral Trench. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|Wat Tambor: Enigmatic anominity personified.|''Attack of the Clones'' concept artist [[Robert E. Barnes]]|''[[The Art of Star Wars Episode II: Attack of the Clones]]''}} [[File:TechnoBaron.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art of Wat Tambor by Michael Murnane.]] Originally created for the [[2002]] film [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], Wat Tambor first appeared in ''[[Cloak of Deception]]'', a [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] novel written by [[James Luceno]]''[[Cloak of Deception]]'' that was released on [[May 29]], [[2001]].{{SWArchive|url=eu/lit/novel/f20010529/index.html|text=Sample ''Cloak of Deception''}} The look of the character was created by concept artist [[Michael Murnane]].{{DB|character|wattambor|Tambor, Wat}} His design was inspired by [[Wikipedia:Art Deco|Art Deco]] style and ''[[Wikipedia:Flash Gordon|Flash Gordon]]'' and is composed of simple shapes and clean lines which relate to each other. One piece of Tambor, finished by Murnane on [[September 29]], [[2000]], with the production code "0044M", varied his design with a red dress instead of blue one and yellow skin.{{WebCite|url=http://lucasmuseum.org/collection/category/costume-and-fashion-design|text=Costume and Fashion Design|work=lucasmuseum.org|archivedate=20170115081003|nolive=1}} Murnane also created a sculpture of Tambor. In the final film he is an entirely computer-generated creation. Tambor was voiced by ''[[Star Wars]]'' sound designer [[Ben Burtt]] in ''Attack of the Clones''.[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars The Complete Season One|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' The Complete Season One]] ("[[Liberty on Ryloth]]" - Featurette) In [[2008]], Burtt listed Tambor as his "favorite ''Star Wars'' robot".{{SWArchive|url=fans/rocks/news20080710.html|text=WALL·E Creators List Fave Robots}} A line of dialogue in the film originally belonging to Poggle the Lesser concerning the production of battle droids was later given to Tambor, explaining that the Techno Union were the builders of most of the new droid army seen in ''Attack of the Clones''. The [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|illustrated screenplay]] of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']] had Tambor in the main room running to the conference room along with Shu Mai after Vader kills San Hill only to be cut down by Vader later on.[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith Illustrated Screenplay'']] In the final cut, Tambor's death scene was cut and can be seen in the deleted scene "Extended Separatist Slaughter." Tambor's cause of death, however, was confirmed by his [[Databank (2014-)|Databank]] entry. Wat Tambor later appeared in the [[The Clone Wars: Season One|first season]] of the animated series ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'', making his first full appearance in the series in the episode "[[Storm Over Ryloth]]", released on [[February 27]], [[2009]].{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode019.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Storm Over Ryloth}} In the episodes, he was voiced by Burtt's long time colleauge [[Matthew Wood]]. The animation model of Tambor by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] from the films doesn't feature any legs and feet and as such the creators of ''The Clone Wars'' moved the character like he "skoots along". The title "Emir" was given to Tambor by ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]] to give him a level of prestige and greater power and to convey that he is greedy and exploitative. Originally Cham Syndulla was to work together with Tambor as a spiritual leader of the Twi'lek who was actually lying to them and would ultimately attempt to dissppear together with Tambor and the stolen gold.{{SW|url=video/liberty-on-ryloth-episode-featurette|text="Liberty on Ryloth" Episode Featurette}} Wood later reprised his role for the series' [[The Clone Wars: Season Seven|seventh season]] ultimately released in [[2020]]. ===Inconsistencies=== The home media episode featurette of "Liberty on Ryloth" and both the [[2015]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' and the [[2016]] reference book ''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia: Updated and Expanded]]'' state that Tambor's homeworld is Skako.''[[Ultimate Star Wars]]'' This conflicts with the [[2019]] reference book
